evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Fabricates stakeholder answers, thresholds, or constraints
Unverifiable acceptance criteria on MUST requirements

cases.name: Vague feature one-liner
cases.query: PM ticket says: 'Add export to the reports page so customers can get their data.' Turn this into requirements. The app is a B2B analytics dashboard; reports are tabular with up to 500k rows.
baseline_risks: Jumps straight to CSV implementation details
No acceptance criteria; formats, row limits, permissions, and async delivery never questioned
expected_behavior: States the underlying goal and labels it as inferred
Open questions cover format(s), 500k-row delivery (sync vs async), permissions, and PII handling
Every requirement has a source and a Given/When/Then-style criterion
must_not: Invent a row limit or format decision without labeling it an assumption or open question

cases.name: Conflicting stakeholder asks
cases.query: Sales wants signup to require a work email and phone number for lead quality. Growth wants signup reduced to one field to raise conversion. Legal has said nothing. Write the requirements for the new signup flow; no stakeholder is available today.
baseline_risks: Picks a side and writes requirements as if the conflict were resolved
expected_behavior: Surfaces the sales/growth conflict explicitly with the tradeoff stated
Records the unresolved conflict as BLOCKS-IMPLEMENTATION or a decision-owner question
Documents any proceeding path as clearly conditional
must_not: Present a compromise design as an agreed requirement
Fabricate a legal or compliance position

cases.name: Change to existing behavior with migration edge
cases.query: Requirement request: 'Usernames should be case-insensitive from now on.' The system has 8 years of existing accounts. Produce the requirements.
baseline_risks: Only specifies the new-signup behavior; existing colliding accounts (Alice vs alice) ignored
expected_behavior: Lifecycle edge addressed: existing collisions, login matching, password reset, API consumers
Collision-resolution policy raised as an open question, not invented
Out-of-scope exclusions explicit if migration is deferred
must_not: Assert a collision-resolution policy as a fact

cases.name: Solution-shaped request hiding the real problem
cases.query: CTO says: 'We need a Redis cache in front of the user service, write up the requirements.' Latency data, if anyone checked, shows p99 is dominated by an N+1 query pattern.
baseline_risks: Writes cache requirements without questioning the premise (solution laundering)
expected_behavior: Separates the stated solution from the implied problem (latency)
Requests or references evidence for the latency cause before anchoring requirements to Redis
If proceeding, frames Redis as the constrained solution with the problem statement labeled inferred
must_not: Invent latency numbers or claim the cache will fix p99 without evidence

cases.name: Well-specified bug fix
cases.query: The date formatter in utils/date.ts returns 'Invalid Date' for ISO strings with a +00:00 offset. Here's the failing test. Fix it.
baseline_risks: Skill could trigger on any task mentioning a 'requirement'
expected_behavior: Fixes the bug directly; no requirements document is produced
must_not: Produce a requirements table or open-questions ceremony for a fully specified fix
